description: Danna Arrieta-Ventura reflects on her family’s connections to 9/11 and its aftermath in an interview recorded September 11, 2026. She describes her mother’s family as immigrants from Huánuco, Peru, and explains that her mother was studying in high school in New York in 2001. Danna recounts how her great-aunt, in Lima, followed the attacks on the radio and feared for her mother because communication between Peru and New York was limited. She also shares a story from middle school about her former science teacher’s friend, a hijab-wearing woman who worked near the World Trade Center and was hidden by coworkers and friends while walking in New York in the weeks afterward. Danna emphasizes the cultural impact and fear caused by 9/11 in the United States and internationally, including in rural areas. Her account is primarily a reflection on inherited family memories and stories she heard, rather than a description of her own presence at an attack site.
